claims.text: The initial material is solution-treated, homogenized, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The initial grain size is approximately 20 µm.
The proposed intervention is aging at 650 °C for 10 h in an inert atmosphere.
Aging will produce approximately 3 vol% coherent L12 γ′ precipitates with sizes of 20–50 nm.
The proposed effect holds for aging temperatures of 600–700 °C and aging times no longer than 10 h.
The proposed effect holds when each alloying-element concentration is within ±2 at.% of the equiatomic composition.
Orowan bowing around the precipitates impedes dislocation motion.
The precipitates blunt crack tips.
Dislocation impediment and crack-tip blunting jointly increase strength and fracture toughness.
Aging will increase yield strength by 20±5% relative to the solution-treated baseline.
Aging will increase ultimate tensile strength by 15±5% relative to the solution-treated baseline.
Aging will increase fracture toughness by 10±3% relative to the solution-treated baseline.
Aging will reduce ductility by less than 5% relative to the solution-treated baseline.
Aging will change Young’s modulus by less than 2% relative to the solution-treated baseline.
The solution-treated baseline yield strength is approximately 300 MPa.
The solution-treated baseline ultimate tensile strength is approximately 550 MPa.
The solution-treated baseline fracture toughness is approximately 60 MPa√m.
The solution-treated baseline elongation is approximately 50%.
The solution-treated baseline Young’s modulus is approximately 200 GPa.
Chromium contents above 15 at.% cause secondary-phase formation and invalidate the proposed effect.

contradictions.description: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi contains approximately 20 at.% Cr, and the allowed ±2 at.% range implies roughly 18–22 at.% Cr, yet the boundary states that the hypothesis fails whenever Cr exceeds 15 at.%.

The headline hypothesis requires a fracture-toughness increase greater than 10%, whereas the predicted range of 10±3% includes values as low as 7% and therefore does not consistently satisfy that requirement.
